touches.text: Lifetimes. Each tree declares its lifetime when it is made: kept, one activity (eg one sleep run), or until its source file changes. Dropping a tree drops its leaves and its own links. A node goes only when no tree indexes it, so whatever a temporary tree's activity promoted into a permanent tree outlives it. The drop is enforced, not a habit. WHY: a run that ends without dropping its tables leaves them behind forever.

Transient things may help debugging out to 30 days and won't be needed past that, eg an inference ticket looked at a week later because a bug turned up. No trouble should stand unresolved at 30 days; sleep's cleanup may be made to spare one that does.
Shareable provenance (charters, tickets, validations) is git JSON beside the code, never a row.

Prebuild face: the chart chain, eight machines, each answering one question before a build begins: orient (what is asked, where does it live), constrain (what bounds it), survey (what already exists), decompose (how does it split), triage (what first, by what standard), hypothesize (what do we expect, how would we know we're wrong), validate (what does DONE mean, measured), and after the build, verdict (what done actually meant).
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
Hollow runs: proves a proof goes red when the build is removed.

Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged. [Q#90: A proof's seal is one record, so the newest OS to seal replaces the other's, and a proof with teeth for both OSes reds on every single OS. Measured 2026-11-12: a Windows reseal of a mixed proof overwrote the Linux seal. Do seals go per OS (validations/<os>/, or an OS key in the record), or is one OS the sealing box?]
Test runs are transient (30 days, 4.3.2); seals are records of truth (git).
TOOLS: base, validation_store, proof_coverage, scratch, question, proof_discovery, chain, bus_client, artifact, system_word; machine build_inspector; db client.
The chart chain machines (9.3.2): orient, constrain, survey, decompose, triage, hypothesize, validate, verdict.
proof_coverage: joins a ticket's falsifier clauses to the proofs that cover them and the seals that ran green. WHY: a falsifier nobody proves is a hypothesis (Law 3). USERS: the tester.

question: the open-question door: a decision only the operator can make, bound to its ticket, answered in the operator's words. WHY: a spec choice is settled by Akien's head, recorded verbatim, never by a paragraph of CC's. USERS: tickets and CodeMother open them; the operator answers (7.4.2).
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.
